# Frozen 1.6.0 outputs

These files contain synthetic inputs and outputs obtained by importing the unchanged, checksum-verified public 1.6.0 source archive outside the maintained Rust source tree. Each imported source file was compared byte-for-byte with Git commit `5202477edfe4b5d8bacfa5b2e9fd6eadd9624f7f`; `core-reference.json` records those source digests. The expected results come from the released implementation, rather than a second implementation of its algorithms.

`released-diagnostics.json` adds the released content-free event schema, bounded retention, exact recorded rounding, invalid-input rejection, safe chronological export and file permissions. It is also exercised by the [joined recording workflow comparison](../../../mluva-workflows/tests/fixtures/README.md).

`config-defaults.json` records all 49 settings. The 357 persisted-setting cases cover migrations, privacy choices, onboarding, provider settings, Unicode character bounds, numeric limits, malformed types and URLs. Accepted cases record the difference from the frozen defaults; rejected cases retain the reference's diagnostic for review. `xdg-paths.json` includes ordinary fallback and explicit empty roots. The 6,540 transcript cases cover command phrases, repeated corrections, sentence and paragraph boundaries, Unicode word boundaries, unusual whitespace and a deterministic synthetic corpus. The compiled `word-ranges.json` resource freezes Unicode 16 word classification observed through the reference runtime's regular-expression engine; transcript cases exercise both ends and neighboring characters of every range through the public normalization function.

Daniel authorized a three-model native lineup on 1 October 2026: Whisper Tiny, Parakeet v3 and Qwen3-ASR 1.7B, keeping Qwen as the default. The frozen settings fixtures are unchanged. Their comparison applies only the authorized retirement delta to Whisper Base/Small; legacy Turbo already migrated in the release. Native file-boundary checks verify migration to Qwen, renewed setup, preservation of other settings, no rewrite during load, successful explicit save and rejection of retired choices for new settings. Existing caches are not deleted.

`history-foundation.sql` is a synthetic database using the original eight-column schema; `released-data.sql` records its migration through the released stores, with source edits, rewrites and a screenshot attachment. `store-baseline.json` captures correction, continuation and merge results, Unicode and literal-wildcard searches, title guards, exact prompt text and a Markdown export. Runtime-generated merge timestamps alone are normalized. The 88 provenance cases cover provider/route combinations, context sources, Unicode model bounds and duration types/bounds. The 82 PNG cases cover truncated chunks, CRC corruption and image dimensions; the tiny image contains only two synthetic colored pixels. `store-reference.json` records source digests for these checks.

The foundational Rust comparisons use Cargo and these static JSON files. Maintained checks do not import or execute Python. Reference collection is temporary development work; its Python script is excluded from the maintained source and final package. External process/platform prerequisites are documented with the respective evidence below.

[Native delivery evidence](delivery-evidence.md) adds 315 independently collected clipboard/insertion sessions and 123 terminal sessions through real disposable native helpers, processes and Unix sockets. The two owning tests protect callback/receipt ordering and exact compositor/process identity, with seven combined delivery cases and actual half-second query failures. These checks require Linux `/proc`; the default daemon-path case additionally requires bubblewrap for a private tmpfs/PID namespace. They exercise no host clipboard or input. Native AT-SPI, actual isolated target insertion and complete workflow assembly remain pending.

`default-prompts.json` in the compiled resources preserves the eleven prompts, five Live templates and seven built-in styles as data. The prompt fixtures include 26 validation cases and ten damaged/valid override reads, including exact UTF-8 repair diagnostics. Sixteen title cases and a bounded request check label behavior without shortening stored source text. Five Scratchpad cases cover legacy defaults and malformed recovery documents. Their imported source digests are recorded in `prompt-reference.json`.

The personalization fixtures record 4,605 dictionary/snippet cases, 11,984 whole-string casing observations, 55 protected-text integrity cases, 63 persisted-document loads and three save/reload traces. They cover longest-phrase order, application scopes, literal replacements, Unicode boundaries, matched capitalization, typed tokens, variables, style selections and explicit vocabulary dismissal. Generated UUIDs are validated as UUIDs and normalized only where the reference also generates them. The persistence checks compare saved JSON formatting and private file modes, preserve malformed documents and reject failed writes without changing live state. Load cases currently compare acceptance and state; exact decoder diagnostics beyond the existing corpus remain part of application acceptance.

`case-properties.json` freezes Unicode 16 character ranges, complete upper/lower mappings and the release runtime's literal ignore-case groups as data. Tests cover range edges, expansions, final Greek sigma and characters added in later Unicode versions. This keeps native library updates from silently changing existing replacement behavior. The Unicode normalization dependency is separately pinned to the matching Unicode 16 tables.

`markdown-cases.json` contains 1,839 restrained-Markdown parsing, visible-projection and wrapping observations, including Unicode line separators, escapes, fences and malformed delimiters. `text-diff-cases.json` records 608 source-edit ranges, including repeated-token tie handling, emoji, punctuation and the large-input fallback. The focused-correction and suggestion fixtures contain 82 and 12 cases respectively; suggestions remain review-only and are derived only from corrections explicitly saved in History. `personalization-reference.json` records source digests and counts for these component checks.
